name: Campaign Tracker
tagline: Platform for tracking and analyzing political campaign spending and advertising in the Netherlands
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on volunteer contributors for maintenance
Limited funding sustainability beyond grant cycles
academic_citations: Boogers, M., & Voerman, G. (2023). Digital transparency in Dutch elections. Journal of E-Democracy, 15(2), 45-62.
policy_outcomes: Increased transparency requirements for political advertising in Dutch electoral law (2023)
Adoption of Campaign Tracker data by Dutch Parliament for campaign finance monitoring
documented_limitations: Coverage limited to major parties and campaigns
Data collection relies on public disclosures which vary in completeness
failure_modes: Delays in official campaign finance reporting
governance_model: nonprofit board with stakeholder advisory council
curation_criteria: Tracks all registered political parties and campaigns meeting electoral thresholds; includes advertising spend, donor information, and media coverage analysis
contributor_governance: Open contribution model with editorial review process for data submissions
community_ownership: Nonprofit governance with public advisory board including journalists, academics, and civil society representatives
controversies: 2022 debate over inclusion of minor party data and potential bias in coverage selection
political_bias_allegations: Allegations of underrepresentation of right-wing parties in early versions (2017-2018), addressed through expanded data collection
legal_regulatory_issues: Operates under Dutch data protection law (GDPR); compliant with campaign finance transparency regulations
government_partnerships: Dutch Electoral Council (Kiesraad) - data sharing agreement
ai_involvement: Limited - uses basic NLP for media monitoring and classification of advertising content
